entries.title: Confirm Send no longer lists every additional contact under CC
entries.summary: With **Include additional contacts of recipients (CC)**, each recipient's additional contacts are copied on that recipient's own email. **Confirm Send** used to merge all of them onto one **CC** line, so a bulk send looked as if every email copied everyone. The **CC** line now shows only the addresses copied on every email, and the per-recipient copies appear as a count: "Additional contacts: N people CC'd on their own contact's email". Delivery was always correct; only the dialog changed.

where.path: Contacts or Sessions → select records → Send → Send Email → Include additional contacts of recipients (CC) → Review → Send Now

entries.use_case: A program team emails 120 speakers with each speaker's assistant CC'd. Confirm Send now reads "Additional contacts: 120 people CC'd on their own contact's email", not a CC line of 120 assistants that makes it look like every assistant gets every speaker's email.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer worries that a bulk email CC'd every additional contact on every message, or hesitates at Confirm Send because the CC line looks wrong.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers who email speakers or contacts with their additional contacts (assistants, co-authors) CC'd.
internal.staff_path: Event → Contacts → select records → Send → Send Email → Include additional contacts of recipients (CC) → Review → Send Now
internal.gotchas: Display-only: emails always went out with each contact's own additional contacts only. A manually typed CC, or a CC that lands on every email, still shows on the CC line. With one recipient everything is listed as before. In Sessions → Select Individual Contacts, only checked recipients are counted. Reported by Clarion (event 6018, SB-10102).
internal.talk_track: What you see at Confirm Send now matches what goes out: each assistant is copied only on their own speaker's email.

entries.title: Session Catalog: choose a Catalog, Timetable or Agenda program layout — with a session panel, People directory and Add to calendar
entries.summary: A Session Catalog gallery now has a **Program layout** setting in the Design tab: **Catalog** (filter rail beside session rows grouped by day and time), **Timetable** (rooms across, start times down, colour-coded by track, with a Grid / List toggle) or **Agenda** (day tabs and expandable rows with Now / Next / Ended chips). Switching is instant in the preview. All three open the same session panel — date, time, room and time zone, abstract, speakers with bios, the presentations inside a symposium, **Save**, **Copy link** and **Add to calendar** (calendar file, Google Calendar, Outlook). A **People** tab adds a faculty directory with person pages. Sessions without a start time collect under a **TBA** day. The **Your brand** theme now keeps a neutral canvas and uses the brand colour for navigation and buttons, and the Site's font is loaded on every gallery.

enable.path: CMS → Content Galleries → a Session Catalog gallery → Design → Program layout

where.path: CMS → Content Galleries → a Session Catalog gallery → Design → Program layout / Navigation tabs → People

entries.use_case: A scientific congress with six rooms and three days wants attendees to scan the day room by room the way they do on the printed grid, and a single-track summit wants a phone-friendly agenda. Both are the same Session Catalog; the organizer picks Timetable or Agenda in Design and the published program, the session panel and Add to calendar come with it.

cs_action.note: Existing Session Catalogs keep the Catalog layout (the previous rows, now with the toolbar and day grouping). Offer Timetable to multi-room programs and Agenda to single-track or mobile-first ones; check the People tab is on if the customer wants a faculty page.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer compares our program page to cAttendee, Oxford Abstracts or a custom program site, asks for a room-by-time grid, a day-tab agenda, speaker bios in the program, a faculty list, or Add to calendar on sessions.
internal.who_should_get_it: Content Galleries preview customers publishing a Session Catalog — medical and scientific programs first.
internal.staff_path: Org → CMS → Content Galleries → a Session Catalog → Design → Program layout; super users can flip Demo mode (account menu) to preview every layout with a generated congress.
internal.gotchas: Timetable falls back to the list under 1024px and on the TBA day. Add to calendar appears only on sessions with a start time. Demo mode data shows only in the builder preview (preview token), never on the public URL. Program strings are English-only until the fr/es/de gallery translations ship. The Your brand theme change affects every gallery on that preset — the canvas is no longer the brand primary.

entries.title: Brella is generally available, and Apps is open to anyone who manages integrations
entries.summary: Brella no longer needs Sessionboard to add it: open **Apps** in the left sidebar, choose **Brella** under **Engagement**, and connect it yourself. **Apps** in the organization sidebar now shows to anyone who can view integrations, not only Sessionboard staff, and organization **Settings > Integrations** opens Apps.
entries.use_case: A customer running their event app on Brella can connect it the same day without a support ticket: their admin opens Apps, adds the Brella token and organization ID, and maps each Sessionboard event to a Brella event. Admins who used to go to Settings > Integrations land on Apps automatically.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer asks for Brella, asks where Settings > Integrations went, or reports that Apps was locked for their admin.
internal.who_should_get_it: Organizations that use Brella for networking or content, and any admin who manages integrations.
internal.gotchas: LiveBuzz is still added by Sessionboard on request. Brella refuses a timeslot outside its event dates, so line those up before the first sync. Nothing is deleted in Brella: a speaker who leaves the accepted set comes off the timeslot and both records stay.
internal.talk_track: Brella is now a self-serve app. Open Apps from the sidebar, connect Brella with your token and organization ID, map your event, and sync.

entries.title: See every email an event will send before it goes out
entries.summary: **Email Campaigns → Upcoming sends** lists the next 7, 14 or 30 days of automatic email: scheduled and recurring campaigns, upload slot, acceptance, call for papers and awards reminders, the speaker feedback release, and date-based automations. Open a send to see each recipient and the email they will get, with a warning when it reaches people on unaccepted sessions. Two automatic sends that were failing now go out: date-based automations that skipped enrolled contacts, and the awards submission deadline reminder.
entries.use_case: Before a reminder goes out, a program manager can check exactly who receives it and what it says, and catch a send that would reach speakers on pending or declined sessions, instead of finding out from a confused speaker afterwards.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer asks why someone got (or did not get) an automatic email, or wants to check reminders before a deadline.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any event team using reminders, scheduled campaigns or automations.
internal.gotchas: The recipient list shows the first 500 people. Automations with no fixed time are listed separately as sends that fire when triggered.
internal.talk_track: Upcoming sends is one list of everything the event will email on its own. Open any send to see who gets it and preview the message.

entries.title: A guided wizard for new sites, galleries and embeds
entries.summary: **Create** on **Publish → Sites** — and **New site**, **New gallery** and **New embed** on the Publish overview — open one short wizard. Pick what you are making (**Marketing Site**, **Session Catalog**, **Media Gallery**, **ePoster Gallery** or **Embed**), name it and choose its web address (the host is shown, the address is checked as you type), then the layout, who can see it and its look. It only asks what that surface needs, and you land in the builder. A surface that is not on yet is greyed out with the reason and a button to turn it on or ask for it.

where.path: Publish → Sites → Create (or New site / New gallery / New embed on Publish → Overview)

entries.use_case: A marketing lead wants an on-demand library for last year's recordings. They click New gallery, pick Media Gallery, type a name and address, choose the On-Demand Hub layout and email-gated access, and land in a builder that is already set up — no blank page, no hunting through settings.

cs_action.note: Good moment to show customers who have put off building a gallery or site.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer asks how to start a site, gallery or embed, or which one they need.
internal.who_should_get_it: Anyone who publishes event content: marketing and program teams.
internal.staff_path: Org or event → Publish → Sites → Create
internal.gotchas: Each event has one marketing site, so on an event that already has one the Marketing Site card says Open the site. Gallery cards are locked until Content Galleries (Preview) is on; ePoster Gallery is locked until Poster Gallery (Beta) is on for the event — at org level, until any live event has it. Session Catalog and ePoster Gallery are per event, so at org level the wizard asks which event.
internal.talk_track: Tell it what you're making and it asks only what that needs, then drops you into a builder that's already set up.

entries.title: Publish: Sites, Embeds and Posters in the sidebar, live previews of every site
entries.summary: The Publish module is simpler. In an event it lists **Overview**, **Sites**, **Embeds** and **Posters** (plus **Floor Maps** when on); at the organization level, **Overview** and **Sites**. Galleries now sit on the **Sites** page under its **Galleries** tab, and every card shows a screenshot of that site's landing page, its own domain or address, and an open-in-new-tab button on hover. **Posters** is always listed and explains Poster Gallery on events that do not have it. The **Overview** gives each row its type icon, shows only the places an item is actually live, drops the empty Views column, renames **Lists** to **Embeds**, leaves out archived and deleted events, and adds **Configure SSO** and **Domains** buttons. In Program, **Collect & Review → Submission forms** is now just **Forms** in the sidebar.
entries.use_case: A program manager opens Publish → Sites and recognises each site from its screenshot instead of a list of slugs, and spots that last year's archived event no longer clutters the Overview.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer can't find Content Galleries or Poster Gallery in the sidebar, or asks where their galleries went.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers with sites, galleries or embeds.
internal.gotchas: The Content Galleries list page still exists at /cms/galleries but has no sidebar row; galleries are reached from the Sites page. Screenshots are captured on first view (2–3 s) and refreshed when the site changes or after 12 hours; until then the card shows a layout sketch. Posters opens the Poster Gallery request page on events without it — it no longer has a lock.
internal.talk_track: Everything with its own address is on one page now, and you can see what each one looks like before you open it.

entries.title: Add Program: one page for conferences, awards, webinars and gatherings
entries.summary: **Add Event** is now **Add Program**, on the organization's **Events** page and under the **+** button. It opens a page that asks **What are you creating?** — **Conference**, **Awards**, **Webinar** or **Gathering** — with tidier basics (**Name**, **Starts**, **Ends**, **Time zone**, **Website**). Webinars and gatherings are marked **Beta** when your organization does not have them yet and show what they do with a **Request beta access** button instead of a form. **Awards** shows your plan's program allowance and **Start the awards wizard**, or **Add-on** with **Talk to us about Awards** when your organization does not have Awards.
entries.use_case: An events lead wants to try a webinar series. Add Program → Webinar shows what webinars do and a Request beta access button, instead of a form they cannot submit.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer asks how to add an event, webinar, gathering or awards program, or why they cannot create a webinar.
internal.who_should_get_it: Every org admin who creates events.
internal.staff_path: Org → Events → Add Program. Super users get a View as customer toggle, a staff-only Advanced panel (sandbox seeding) and Create anyway on gated kinds.
internal.gotchas: The Lite conference format is gone from this page. Webinar/Gathering need the gatherings Beta; requests for it go through Early Access. Super users see staff-only controls — use View as customer to demo it.
internal.talk_track: Pick what you are making and the page asks only what that needs — and tells you plainly when something needs to be turned on first.

entries.title: Conference requests ask the onboarding questions and reach Customer Success directly
entries.summary: When a new conference has to be set up by Customer Success, **Add Program** now sends a request that asks **Help us set it up**: what you manage (abstracts, sessions or both), roughly how many speakers and sessions, whether submissions are evaluated (rounds and evaluators), and when the call opens and closes — all optional. The confirmation, ready and declined emails come from the Customer Success team's address, so a reply reaches them. Customer Success sees the request, with those answers, the moment it is sent and can open it straight into a prefilled event form.

where.path: Events → Add Program → Conference → Send request

entries.use_case: A society contracted for one meeting requests a second. Their request says ~120 speakers, two evaluation rounds and a call closing 20 February, so their CSM can scope the contract change and set the event up toward those dates without a separate intake call.

cs_action.note: CS handles requests from the success@ inbox and the Event requests section of Admin → Onboarding intake; nothing to enable.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer asks for a new event, or a single-event customer wants to add one.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers who cannot create conferences themselves (most orgs).
internal.staff_path: Admin → Onboarding intake → Event requests → open a request → Open in Add Program form / Open in clone form → Create and fulfil request (or Decline, reason optional). The internal email to success@ has the same link; replying to it answers the requester.
internal.gotchas: There is no contract or entitlement check — any org member who can open Add Program can request, and the CSM decides. The setup questions are asked only for conferences, not webinars or gatherings. Fulfilling adds the requester to the event's team.
internal.talk_track: Tell us roughly what the event looks like when you ask for it, and your CSM can get it set up — and your plan sorted — without a separate call.

entries.title: Starting an awards program no longer errors when your plan has none left
entries.summary: Clicking **New Program** in Awards, or **Awards** on **Add Program**, used to show an error when your plan allowed no more awards programs. It now opens a panel that shows how many programs your plan includes and how many you have used, with **Start the awards wizard** — or, when none are left (or none are included yet), says so plainly and offers **Contact Customer Success**.

where.path: Awards → New Program (or Events → Add Program → Awards)

entries.use_case: An admin whose plan includes three awards programs, all used, sees "You've used all 3" and a way to contact their CSM, instead of an error that looks like a bug.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer reports an error when creating an awards program.
internal.who_should_get_it: Awards customers at or near their program allowance.
internal.staff_path: Org → Awards → New Program; the allowance is the org plan’s Max awards programs.
internal.gotchas: An org whose plan has Max awards programs empty or 0 sees "Your plan doesn't include awards programs yet" even with the Awards module on — raise the plan limit to let them create one. Starting the wizard needs the Create Awards permission.
internal.talk_track: If your plan is full, it tells you so and how to get more — no mystery error.

entries.title: Organization Home shows your upcoming events; the new dashboard is on for everyone
entries.summary: The organization's **Home** page now shows your upcoming events right under **Needs you**, each card a click into the event. The redesigned organization **Dashboard** is now on for every organization, not only those using Pathways; the Pathways and Topics cards still appear only when Pathways is on.
entries.use_case: An admin who runs six events a year opens Home and jumps straight into the one starting next week from its card.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer asks for a faster way into their events, or notices the dashboard changed.
internal.gotchas: The event dashboard is unchanged. Admin Settings (org and event) no longer list the retired Community, New Navigation, Setup Center and Briefs toggles — display only, their stored values are untouched.
internal.talk_track: Your next events are on Home, a click away.

entries.title: Domains lists only events that send from their own address
entries.summary: **Settings > Domains** at the organization level listed every event under **Event email addresses**, including events that simply use the organization's address. It now lists only events that send from their own address, and hides the table when none do.
entries.use_case: An admin checking which events need their own domain set up sees only the two events that send from their own address, not every event repeating the organization's address.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer is confused that every event appears to have its own sender address.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers with a custom email domain.
internal.gotchas: Case or surrounding spaces do not make an address different. An event whose own domain setup is in progress still appears.
internal.talk_track: The list now shows only events that really send from somewhere else.

entries.title: Content Galleries now include a Program page with agenda, catalog, and timetable views
entries.summary: A **Program** page is now available inside Content Galleries, giving attendees three ways to browse sessions: an **Agenda** view (day-by-day list), a **Catalog** view (card grid), and a **Timetable** grid. Each view includes a **Filter** dropdown, day tabs, pagination, and a **Session Drawer** that opens full session details — including speaker avatars, session chips, and calendar-link actions — without leaving the page. A **People** page listing speakers is also included, with individual speaker profile pages.

enable.path: Get started → Early Access → Preview → Content Galleries

where.path: Content Galleries → gallery → Program page; Content Galleries → gallery → People page

entries.use_case: An organizer publishing a Content Gallery can now surface the full event program — sessions, speakers, times, and rooms — directly inside the gallery so attendees can browse, filter, and add sessions to their calendar without navigating away. This replaces the need to maintain a separate program site or embed just for session discovery.

cs_action.note: Feature is in Preview; customers must opt in via Early Access. Confirm the gallery has sessions and speaker data populated before demoing.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks how to publish their agenda or speaker list publicly, or wants a single attendee-facing destination for both program and content.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers already using or evaluating Content Galleries who want to expose their session schedule to attendees.
internal.staff_path: Content Galleries → open a gallery → Program or People page tab
internal.gotchas: A demo mode file (demoProgram.ts) is included in the codebase — confirm it is not surfaced to real customers in production. The PR title says 'QA fixes' but the diff is almost entirely new components; treat this as a new feature launch, not a patch.
internal.talk_track: Your gallery can now be the single link you share with attendees — they get the full agenda with filters and a timetable, plus speaker profiles, all in the same branded experience as your on-demand content.

draft.docs_gap: The /site/content-galleries guide should add a section documenting the Program page (Agenda, Catalog, and Timetable views), the People page, the Session Drawer, and how session data flows from the event into the gallery.
draft.why_use_it: Content Galleries bring your event's sessions, speakers, and on-demand content together in a single branded destination. The Program page lets attendees explore what is happening, filter by track or format, and get session details in a side drawer — all without leaving the gallery. Use it when you want one URL that covers both the live program and recorded content.

entries.title: Request and configure the Attend Mobile App from Early Access and Event Admin Settings
entries.summary: A new **Attend Mobile App** card appears in **Early Access → Beta** so event admins can raise a hand for the feature. Once the toggle is enabled for an event via **Event Admin Settings → Early Access**, the **App Sign-In Settings** panel appears directly below the feature list, letting admins choose sign-in methods for the attendee app without needing the full Attend module enabled.

enable.path: Get started → Early Access → Beta → Attend Mobile App (request); then Event Admin Settings → Early Access → Attend Mobile App (toggle on)

where.path: Early Access → Beta → Attend Mobile App; Event Admin Settings → Early Access → App Sign-In Settings

entries.use_case: An event admin who wants to offer a branded mobile app experience can request access to the Attend Mobile App from Early Access and, once enabled, configure how attendees sign in — all from Event Admin Settings, before the full Attend module is live.

cs_action.note: The attend_app toggle only appears in Event Admin Settings once the API's available_features includes it (web-api #4518). CSMs or support must ensure that backend flag is live before the toggle shows up for the customer.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks about a mobile attendee app, wants to offer app-based check-in, or is evaluating Attend.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers running in-person or hybrid events who want a mobile app experience for attendees.
internal.staff_path: Event Admin Settings → Early Access → Attend Mobile App toggle; Attend → Attendee App page (visible to non-staff once attend_app is on)
internal.gotchas: The toggle in Event Admin Settings only appears after the backend available_features flag is set via web-api #4518. Without that, the Early Access card shows but the toggle does not. Non-staff admins can now see the App Sign-In Settings panel whenever the event has attend_app enabled — previously it was super-user only.
internal.talk_track: You can request the Attend Mobile App right from Early Access, and once it is turned on for your event you configure attendee sign-in options in Event Admin Settings — no need to wait for the full Attend module to be enabled.

draft.docs_gap: The Early Access guide should document the Attend Mobile App Beta card and explain that enabling the toggle in Event Admin Settings surfaces the App Sign-In Settings panel.
draft.why_use_it: The Attend Mobile App gives attendees a dedicated app experience for your event, letting them browse the agenda, find sessions, and sign in with the methods you choose. You configure sign-in options directly in Event Admin Settings as soon as the feature is enabled for your event, so setup happens on your schedule. Requesting access through Early Access puts you in the queue and lets you preview what the app offers before it is broadly available.

entries.title: Attend app sends push notifications when a session's time or room changes
entries.summary: The Attend mobile app now sends push notifications to registered attendees when a session's scheduled time or room is updated. Notifications are delivered in the attendee's device locale (English, German, Spanish, or French), respect a configurable quiet window (default 22:00–07:00 in the event's timezone), and are capped at three per attendee per day. The feature is controlled by a new per-event setting **push_session_changes** (off by default); a UI toggle in the Event app settings panel is coming in a follow-up release.

enable.path: Ask your Customer Success Manager to enable push_session_changes for your event; then Event Settings → App Settings → push_session_changes

where.path: Attend mobile app (attendee device) — push notification received automatically when a session time or room changes

entries.use_case: When a session moves rooms or shifts time slots, every attendee with the Attend app installed gets an instant push notification — no email needed, no attendee left hunting for the change on the day of the event. Organizers can turn this on per event once their mobile app is live.

cs_action.note: The push_session_changes setting defaults to off. A UI toggle is not yet in the web app — enabling requires a direct API PUT or Sessionboard Support action. Also, ATTEND_PUSH_PROVIDER must be set to 'expo' in Doppler for the US region; EU and ME regions remain 'none' until a sub-processor decision is made. iOS delivery also requires APNs credentials in EAS (not yet configured), so iOS pushes will fail until that is set up.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer using the Attend app asks how attendees will be notified of last-minute schedule changes, or when they report attendees missing room or time updates.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers actively using the Attend mobile app in the US region; EU and ME customers must wait for the sub-processor decision on Expo.
internal.staff_path: Event Settings → App Settings → push_session_changes (via API until the UI toggle ships)
internal.gotchas: EU and ME regions have ATTEND_PUSH_PROVIDER=none by default — no pushes are sent there until a Doppler change is made after the sub-processor review. iOS delivery requires APNs credentials in EAS (Apple Developer account not yet set up); Android requires FCM credentials in EAS. The web UI toggle for push_session_changes has not shipped yet. Pushes go to every live registrant with a phone — there is no saved-agenda narrowing until a saved-agenda table exists. Quiet hours default to 22:00–07:00 in the event's timezone; deferred pushes are released by a 5-minute sweep cron.
internal.talk_track: When a session moves rooms or shifts time, the Attend app pushes a notification straight to every attendee's phone — no email, no app refresh needed. It respects quiet hours and caps at three notifications per attendee per day, so it stays useful without becoming noise.

draft.docs_gap: The notifications guide should add a section covering Attend app push notifications: how to enable push_session_changes, quiet-hour and daily-cap behaviour, locale support, and the EU/ME provider status.
draft.why_use_it: Push notifications in the Attend app keep attendees informed of last-minute schedule changes without requiring them to check email or refresh the app. When a session's time or room changes, the app delivers a notification directly to the attendee's device in their preferred language. Quiet hours and a daily cap prevent notification fatigue, so attendees stay informed without being overwhelmed.

entries.title: Attend app: Credits tab shows earned credits, claim links and certificates
entries.summary: The **Credits** tab in the Attend app now loads for attendees. It shows every session that carries continuing-education credit, each session's credit status (**Earned**, **Claimable**, **Needs Attendance**, **Not Open**, etc.), a running **Offered / Earned / Remaining** total per credit type, a signed link to the claim site when a session is claimable, and a signed certificate link for every credit already earned. When the event has not enabled credits, the tab returns an empty state immediately.

enable.path: Ask your Customer Success Manager to enable Credits and the Attend app for your event; then open the Attend app and navigate to the Credits tab

entries.use_case: Attendees at CE-eligible events can open the Credits tab in the Attend app to see exactly which sessions they attended, what credits they have already earned, and where to claim credits they have not yet collected — without leaving the app to hunt for a separate claim site link.

cs_action.note: Both the Credits feature flag and the Attend app (beta) must be on for the event. The Credits tab is only visible when the event-level 'credits' flag is enabled (default off).

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer running CE-eligible events asks how attendees can track or claim credits from a mobile or web app experience.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers who use Lessons & Credits and have the Attend app enabled — typically medical, legal, or professional-development conferences.
internal.staff_path: Attend app → Credits tab (visible to the attendee after token-based sign-in)
internal.gotchas: Claiming itself still happens on the separate CE claim site (/learn/:storefrontId/claim); the app only provides a signed link into it. If magic links are disabled for the storefront, the claim URL is not shown. A registration transfer clears the person_id link, so a transferred attendee falls back to email lookup — their credits are still visible but the link is unsigned until they identify on the claim site. Draft sessions and archived credit types are excluded. Subsessions appear only when their parent session is public.
internal.talk_track: Attendees open the Credits tab in the Attend app, see every CE-eligible session with its status, tap Claim to go straight to the claim site pre-authenticated, and download their certificate — all without emailing your team.

draft.docs_gap: The article index has no guide covering the Attend app's Credits tab; the closest article is /marketing/attendee-view, but it does not describe the Credits tab, credit status labels, claim links, or certificate downloads — a dedicated section or new guide should be added.
draft.why_use_it: The Credits tab gives attendees a single place to track their continuing-education progress throughout an event. It surfaces earned totals by credit type, surfaces the claim site with a pre-authenticated link when a session is claimable, and delivers signed certificate links the moment a claim is processed — so attendees spend less time chasing paperwork and more time in sessions.

entries.title: Attend app: search for events or enter a code on the "Find your event" screen
entries.summary: The Attend mobile app's **Find your event** screen now searches published events by name and resolves a typed event code to the correct region. Typing three or more characters returns matching current and upcoming events (name, dates, location, logo); typing or pasting an event ID opens that event directly, even after it has ended. Results are limited to events where the Attend app is enabled and the event is not archived, deleted, or a template.

enable.path: Event Settings → Attend app → Enable Attend app

where.path: Attend mobile app → Find your event

entries.use_case: Attendees who download the Attend app can type a few letters of the event name or paste an event code to find and open their event immediately, without needing a direct link from the organizer.

cs_action.note: The Attend app setting (attend_app_settings.enabled) must be turned on for an event before it appears in the directory. This setting is tied to PR #4508, which is noted as unreleased at the time of this PR.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks how attendees will find their event in the Attend mobile app, or when onboarding a customer who wants to use the Attend app for participant-facing content.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using the Attend app (beta) who wants attendees to self-serve finding their event.
internal.gotchas: Events only appear in search if attend_app_settings.enabled is true and the event is not archived, deleted, a template, or under an archived org. The directory search requires at least 3 characters; fewer returns an empty list. The event code lookup (by ID) has no date cutoff and will open ended events. Rate limits apply: 300 searches / 15 min and 120 lookups / 15 min per IP. The attend_app_settings table is tied to PR #4508, which was unreleased at merge time — confirm that PR is live before directing customers to this feature.
internal.talk_track: Attendees open the Attend app, type a few letters of your event name or paste the event code, and they are in — no link required. You control whether your event shows up by toggling the Attend app setting on.

draft.docs_gap: No guide currently covers the Attend app's event directory or the attend_app_settings toggle that controls event visibility; a dedicated Attend app setup guide should document how to enable an event for the directory and what attendees see on the Find your event screen.
draft.why_use_it: The Attend app gives participants a mobile home for the events they attend — agenda, sessions, and more — all in one place. The event directory lets them find any published event by name or code the moment they open the app, so they are never stuck waiting for a link. Organizers control which events appear by toggling the Attend app setting on their event.

entries.title: Save moments from live captions in the Attend app
entries.summary: Attendees in the Attend app can now save individual caption fragments from a live session as **Saved Moments**, optionally add a personal note, and retrieve them later — per session or across the whole event. Moments persist even when the caption is still in transit: if the fragment has not yet been finalised, the text is captured as soon as it is. Notes can be edited or cleared at any time, and moments are deleted automatically when a session or attendee record is removed.

where.path: Attend app → Live Captions → Save Moment

entries.use_case: An attendee in a medical or technical session can tap to save any caption fragment they want to revisit — no screenshot needed. After the session they can review all their saved moments, with personal notes, from a single list covering the whole event.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer asks how attendees can capture or recall specific statements from live-captioned sessions, or when demoing the Attend app's live-captions feature to a medical, legal, or technical conference organizer.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using the Attend app with Live Transcribe enabled for attendee-facing captions.
internal.staff_path: Attend app → session → Live Captions screen
internal.gotchas: Cap is 500 saved moments per attendee per session; the event-wide list returns at most 2000. If a caption fragment was interim or was re-processed when the save was queued, the moment is still created but caption text will be null. Rate limiting is intentionally absent because venue Wi-Fi shares egress IPs. Caption text and note content are redacted from Sentry logs. The companion mobile PR must also ship before attendees see the UI.
internal.talk_track: Attendees can tap to save any caption that matters to them — a drug dosage, a key finding, a speaker quote — and add a private note right in the app. Everything they saved is waiting for them after the session, organised by event.

draft.docs_gap: The Live Transcribe guide covers the organizer and AV-crew setup but does not document the attendee-facing Saved Moments feature; it should add a section explaining how attendees save, annotate, and review moments from the Attend app.
draft.why_use_it: Live captions in the Attend app let attendees follow along in real time, but important statements can scroll past before anyone can act on them. Saved Moments lets attendees bookmark any caption fragment with a tap and attach a private note for context. Moments are organised by session and by event, so attendees can review everything they flagged without leaving the app. Caption text and notes are never logged or shared with other attendees or organizers.

entries.title: Sign in to the Attend app with SSO (OIDC or SAML)
entries.summary: Organizers can now add **SSO** as a sign-in method for the Attend mobile app alongside magic link. In **Attend App Settings**, choose an OIDC or SAML identity provider already linked to the organization; attendees who are registered for the event can then authenticate through that IdP. The app receives a short-lived, single-use code — no token is ever placed in a URL — and the resulting session follows the same three-refresh SSO rule as admin SSO sessions.

enable.path: Event → Settings → Attend App Settings → Sign-in Methods → SSO → select Identity Provider

where.path: Event → Settings → Attend App Settings → Sign-in Methods

entries.use_case: An enterprise event requires all attendees to authenticate through the company's corporate IdP before accessing the Attend app. Enabling SSO as the sign-in method means attendees use their existing corporate credentials — no separate magic link needed — and access is automatically revoked when their IdP account is deactivated.

cs_action.note: The org must already have an OIDC or SAML IdP configured under SSO settings. The web-ui relay's SSO_ALLOWED_REDIRECT_ORIGINS env var must include https://attend.sessionboard.com — confirm with engineering before enabling for a customer.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer using Attend also has SSO enforced for their org and wants attendees to sign in with corporate credentials.
internal.who_should_get_it: Enterprise customers with an existing OIDC or SAML IdP linked to their Sessionboard org who are also using the Attend app (beta).
internal.staff_path: Event → Settings → Attend App Settings → Sign-in Methods → SSO
internal.gotchas: WorkOS, HubSpot, and OAuth2-password IdPs are not supported. A SAML assertion that fails passport validation (bad signature, domain rejection) currently lands on the admin SSO error page rather than returning the attendee to the app. IdP single logout does not end attendee sessions — sessions expire after three token refreshes. Both the web-api PR #4513 and the companion web-ui relay PR must be deployed together; until both are live, attend SSO redirects to the admin SSO error page.
internal.talk_track: If your organization already uses SSO for Sessionboard admins, you can extend that same IdP to your Attend app attendees — they tap 'Sign in with SSO', authenticate through your corporate identity provider, and land straight in the app. No magic links, no separate passwords.

draft.docs_gap: The SSO guide covers admin/organizer SSO setup but does not mention configuring SSO as an Attend mobile app sign-in method; it should add a section explaining how to select an IdP in Attend App Settings and the attendee sign-in flow.
draft.why_use_it: The Attend mobile app gives registered attendees a personalized event experience on their phone. Offering SSO as a sign-in method lets organizations enforce their existing identity policies — single sign-on, MFA, and automatic deprovisioning — without asking attendees to manage a separate credential. It works with any OIDC or SAML provider already connected to the organization, so setup is a single setting change rather than a new integration.

entries.title: Attend app: per-event attendee sign-in with magic link
entries.summary: Confirmed attendees can now sign in to the Sessionboard Attend mobile app using a magic link sent to their registered email address. A 6-digit code in the same email lets them sign in from a different device. Admins enable the feature per event and choose which auth methods to allow via the **Attend App Settings** API endpoint (`PUT /attend/event/:eventId/app/settings`). No event is affected until an admin explicitly turns it on. The org-portal refresh-token scope bug — where a portal refresh token could be mistaken for an admin token — is also fixed.

enable.path: Ask your Customer Success Manager to enable Attend app sign-in for your event; then PUT /attend/event/:eventId/app/settings with { "enabled": true, "authMethods": ["magic_link"] }

where.path: Attend mobile app → event sign-in screen

entries.use_case: Event teams running the Attend mobile app can let confirmed attendees sign in to their event without needing a separate credential — the attendee enters their registered email, receives a magic link and 6-digit code, and is in within seconds. Only people already on the attendee list can sign in, so access stays controlled.

cs_action.note: No event is affected by default. An admin must PUT /attend/event/:eventId/app/settings with enabled:true before any attendee can sign in. There is no UI for this yet — it is API-only.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer is piloting or asking about the Attend mobile app and wants attendees to be able to sign in.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers actively using or evaluating the Attend mobile app (beta).
internal.staff_path: PUT /attend/event/:eventId/app/settings — API only, no admin UI yet.
internal.gotchas: Sign-in is limited to contacts with an Attendees row in confirmed or checked_in status. Unknown email addresses receive a 200 with no email (silent fail) to prevent enumeration. Five wrong code attempts revoke all live links for that registration. At most 5 magic links per registration per 15 minutes. The ATTEND_APP_LINK_BASE_URL env var defaults to https://attend.sessionboard.com. The org-portal refresh-token scope fix is a security correction bundled in this PR — no customer action needed.
internal.talk_track: Attendees open the Attend app, find their event, enter their registration email, and tap the link in the email — or type the 6-digit code if they're reading it on a laptop. Only people already on your attendee list can get in, and each token is locked to that one event.

draft.docs_gap: The /marketing/attendee-view guide does not cover the Attend mobile app sign-in flow, magic-link authentication for attendees, or the per-event app settings endpoint. It should add a section explaining how to enable attendee sign-in, how the magic-link and code flow works, and the security limits (attempt caps, token expiry).
draft.why_use_it: The Attend app gives attendees a mobile experience tied to the event they are registered for. Magic-link sign-in means attendees never create a password — they authenticate with the email address they registered under, and a time-limited link or short code gets them in. Access is scoped strictly to the event the attendee is registered for, so one attendee cannot reach another event's data.
